evidence_snippets: “Vaccine efficacy (VE) against WHO-defined classical pertussis (≥21 days of paroxysmal cough) was 85% (95% CI: 66, 93) for the aP antigens contained in Tetraxim, Pentaxim, and Hexaxim and 96% (95% CI: 86, 99) for the DTwP vaccine (median follow-up period of 1.58 years, ranging from 0.01 to 4.25 years) [51].”

“In a recent evaluation of the real-world effectiveness of aP vaccines in Sweden, the various aP vaccines (including the aP antigens used in Pentaxim and Hexaxim) used since 1996 continued to show high effectiveness, sustained at 95 - 97% between 2007 and 2018 [52,53].”

“From 2011 to 2014, among 192 children < 1 year of age who were hospitalized with confirmed pertussis in Mexico, ≥2 doses of aP vaccine were associated with a reduction in the number of pertussis cases, and no case of pertussis was detected among infants who had received three doses [54].”

“Furthermore, analyses of the nationwide data on pertussis surveillance in Mexico (2008-2019) demonstrated that three doses of Pentaxim or Hexaxim elicited 97.2% protection against laboratory-confirmed pertussis, a value comparable to that observed for the wP vaccine (96.4%) [55].”
key_data_points: Pertussis vaccine efficacy (WHO-defined classical pertussis): 85% (95% CI 66–93) for aP antigens used in Tetraxim/Pentaxim/Hexaxim; comparator DTwP VE 96% (95% CI 86–99); median follow-up 1.58 years (range 0.01–4.25).
Sweden real-world effectiveness of aP vaccines (including aP antigens used in Pentaxim/Hexaxim): 95–97% (2007–2018).
Mexico hospitalized confirmed pertussis cases (<1 year): among 192 cases (2011–2014), no pertussis detected among infants who had received 3 doses.
Mexico nationwide surveillance (2008–2019): 3 doses Pentaxim/Hexaxim protection against laboratory-confirmed pertussis 97.2% (wP 96.4%).
study_population: Infants/children in efficacy trial setting (Senegal RCT, 1990–1994) and real-world national/hospital surveillance populations in Sweden (2007–2018 effectiveness) and Mexico (infants <1 year hospitalized 2011–2014; nationwide surveillance 2008–2019).

evidence_snippets: “There is also a lack of published efficacy data for DT2aP-IPV-Hib-HBV, this is of particular importance due to this hexavalent vaccine only containing 2 pertussis components. A study from Sweden in the 1990s demonstrated that after three doses in infancy, the efficacy of the vaccines with respect to pertussis linked to a laboratory-confirmed case of pertussis or contact with an infected household member with paroxysmal cough for ≥ = 21 days was 58.9% for an experimental two-component aP vaccine (95% CI 50.9 to 65.9), 85.2% for an experimental five-component aP vaccine (95% CI, 80.6 to 88.8), and 48.3% for the licensed whole-cell vaccine (95% CI, 37.0 to 57.6) [66].”
key_data_points: Pertussis vaccine efficacy after 3 infant doses (endpoint: lab-confirmed pertussis or household contact with paroxysmal cough ≥21 days): 58.9% for experimental 2-component aP (95% CI 50.9–65.9); 85.2% for experimental 5-component aP (95% CI 80.6–88.8); 48.3% for licensed whole-cell vaccine (95% CI 37.0–57.6).
Paper notes: “lack of published efficacy data for DT2aP-IPV-Hib-HBV” (Hexaxim).
study_population: Infants (Sweden, 1990s pertussis efficacy study referenced; after three doses in infancy).

Healthy Thai children followed from an RCT: hexavalent (DTaP-IPV-HB-Hib) vs pentavalent (DTwP-HB-Hib) primary series at 2, 4, 6 months and first booster at 18 months; all received Tdap-IPV second booster at 4 years; followed to 6 years.

evidence_snippets: “routine infant vaccination with DT3aP-HBV-IPV/Hib had a beneficial impact on pertussis incidence during 10 years in Australia.”

“Retrospective studies showed that in Italy, where DT3aP-HBV-IPV/Hib has been almost exclusively used since 2001 and vaccination coverage increased from 83.4% in 2002 to >95% by 2011, pertussis-related hospitalization rates progressively decreased from 1.23 to 0.64 per 100,000 inhabitants between 2001 and 2014.”

“Vaccine effectiveness of DT3aP combination vaccines (both pentavalent and hexavalent vaccines) against pertussis hospitalizations was 100% (95% CI: 97.9%–100%) following a 3 + 1 vaccination course in infants in a nationwide study in Switzerland.”

“The estimated effectiveness of hexavalent vaccines (DT3aP-HBV-IPV/Hib and Hexavac) against Hib was 90.4% after 3-dose primary vaccination and 100% post-toddler dose in a nationwide surveillance German study.”
“In a case-control study in the Netherlands, vaccine effectiveness of DT3aP-HBV-IPV/Hib against Hib was 94.0% (95% CI: 89.0%–96.8%), but waned with age.”

“After hexavalent vaccine implementation into immunization programs in Italy, Hib-related hospitalization rates declined from 5.4 to 2.4 per 100,000 population among infants and from 2.3 to 0.9 per 100,000 population among 1–4-year-old children between 2001 and 2005.”

“The impact of hexavalent vaccine implementation on disease incidence was shown for DT3aP-HBV-IPV/Hib (2, 4 and 6 months of age) in Australia, where the overall incidence of HBV decreased from 33.1 to 24.2 cases per 100,000 population between 2009 and 2018.”
key_data_points: Pertussis hospitalization vaccine effectiveness (DT3aP combination vaccines incl. hexavalent/pentavalent), Switzerland, infants, 3+1 course: 100% (95% CI: 97.9%–100%)
Pertussis-related hospitalization rates, Italy: 1.23 to 0.64 per 100,000 inhabitants (2001–2014) with DT3aP-HBV-IPV/Hib almost exclusively used since 2001
Hib effectiveness (DT3aP-HBV-IPV/Hib and Hexavac), Germany: 90.4% after 3-dose primary; 100% post-toddler dose
Hib vaccine effectiveness (DT3aP-HBV-IPV/Hib), Netherlands: 94.0% (95% CI: 89.0%–96.8%); waned with age
Hib-related hospitalization rates, Italy: infants 5.4 to 2.4 per 100,000; ages 1–4 years 2.3 to 0.9 per 100,000 (2001–2005)
HBV incidence, Australia (DT3aP-HBV-IPV/Hib 2,4,6 months): 33.1 to 24.2 cases per 100,000 population (2009–2018)
study_population: Infants/children in post-marketing or observational settings: Switzerland (infants, nationwide study; pertussis hospitalizations), Germany (nationwide surveillance; Hib effectiveness), Netherlands (case-control; Hib effectiveness), Italy (retrospective hospitalization rate trends for pertussis and Hib), Australia (population-level incidence trends for pertussis and HBV).
Healthy Indian toddlers aged 12–24 months receiving a booster dose of HEXASIIL® vs Pentavac SD + Poliovac

Healthy children in Germany aged 4–5 years previously vaccinated with four doses of hexavalent DTPa-HBV-IPV/Hib (Infanrix hexa™) in infancy/second year of life; received a monovalent hepatitis B vaccine challenge dose.

evidence_snippets: Use of Hib conjugate vaccines has led to dramatic declines of >90% in invasive Hib disease in the countries which have included these vaccines in national immunization programmes.

Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and observational studies of the clinical effectiveness of Hib vaccines against meningitis, pneumonia and other forms of invasive Hib disease have demonstrated that Hib vaccine effectively protects against these diseases.

Major declines in levels of nasopharyngeal Hib colonization have also been observed following introduction of Hib conjugate vaccines. This has led to substantially greater reduction in disease incidence than can be directly attributed to the effects of the vaccine, suggesting that widespread use of the vaccine has resulted in the induction of herd protection.
Data from 6 cohort studies suggests that starting vaccination at an older age may lead to higher vaccine effectiveness against invasive Hib disease.

Available data suggest that after 5 years of use of Hib conjugate vaccines, using a 3p+0 schedule, a sustained reduction in meningitis in young children has occurred in a number of developing countries.

A recent evaluation from 4 South American countries reported that Hib meningitis rates were similar 6–10 years after introduction of the vaccine in countries where booster doses were used and in those where boosters were not used.
key_data_points: Impact/effectiveness: >90% declines in invasive Hib disease after introduction in national immunization programmes
Outcome: reduced nasopharyngeal Hib colonization (herd protection suggested)
Population/schedule note: older age at start may increase vaccine effectiveness (6 cohort studies; no numeric estimate provided)
Duration/impact: sustained reduction in meningitis in young children after 5 years of 3p+0 use (no numeric estimate provided)
Comparative impact: Hib meningitis rates similar 6–10 years post-introduction in 4 South American countries with vs without booster (no numeric estimate provided)
study_population: General populations in countries introducing Hib conjugate vaccines (including developing countries; evaluation includes 4 South American countries); children/infants targeted for routine immunization
Children aged 6 years and younger receiving primary pertussis vaccination (whole-cell or acellular) in included studies (systematic review focused on adverse events within 72 hours post-vaccination).
